purpose: Current provenance boundary for physical parameter claims that are not yet strong enough to populate the accepted registry. This file is not consumed by synthesis.
promotion_rule: A claim is promoted only when it resolves to the current reference assembly, matches the registry parameter definition, has reproducible evidence, and has no unresolved conflicting source.

sources.scope: board topology, MCU/IMU/driver/module identity, connector and signal routing
system concept and reaction-wheel construction description

sources.artifact: 自平衡独轮机器人原理剖析及调试笔记.pdf
sources.scope: legacy motor, encoder, control, and operating claims
legacy timer decode, sign conventions, control loop, and MPU6050 register configuration
frame geometry only; no material, component masses, or assembly placement

sources.artifact: prior product-documentation screenshots summarized in project chat
sources.scope: candidate platform dimensions, mass, battery, reaction-wheel geometry, and motor brochure claims

candidate_claims.reason: secondary-only claim and not verified on the current assembled reference unit
13 x 19 = 247, not 241; the document is arithmetically inconsistent and does not unambiguously bind the stated revolution to the current controlled mechanical shaft
legacy software sign is not a measurement of the current robot-positive mechanical direction
line count is not STM32 counter counts per mechanical revolution; legacy and current firmware also use different edge/decode semantics
the 140 g value is the BLDC motor mass, not the reaction-wheel mass
maximum motor torque is not command-to-torque gain and does not characterize the current unit
secondary-only claim conflicts with the 0.0385 N*m legacy motor claim and still is not command-to-torque gain
rated torque is not command-to-torque gain and the primary product source is not in the current source bundle

auxiliary_evidence.use: qualitative inertia-shape evidence only; insufficient for mass or inertia promotion

auxiliary_evidence.use: geometry cross-check only; STL units, body-frame registration, material density, and assembly completeness must be established before deriving body mass properties

promotion_requirements.body.mass_kg: weigh the current assembled reference unit using the same mass partition used by the plant model
promotion_requirements.body.com_height_m: measure/derive center of mass relative to the model body origin with the rotating-wheel mass partition explicitly respected
promotion_requirements.body.inertia_*: derive from verified geometry and component masses or identify with a pendulum/inertia experiment on the current assembly
promotion_requirements.drive_wheel.radius_m: measure the model-relevant effective rolling radius on the installed wheel
promotion_requirements.drive_wheel.mass_kg: weigh the drive-wheel component according to the plant mass partition
promotion_requirements.drive_wheel.spin_inertia_kg_m2: derive from verified geometry/mass or identify experimentally
promotion_requirements.drive_wheel.encoder_*: mark the controlled mechanical shaft, rotate exactly one mechanical revolution both directions under the actual runtime decode mode, then establish sign and a speed/sample bound
promotion_requirements.reaction_wheel.mass_kg: weigh the reaction wheel itself, excluding the motor unless the plant partition is explicitly changed
promotion_requirements.reaction_wheel.com_height_m: measure the reaction-wheel center relative to the model body origin on the assembled robot
promotion_requirements.reaction_wheel.inertia_*: derive from verified wheel geometry/mass or identify experimentally
promotion_requirements.reaction_wheel.encoder_*: measure counts per mechanical revolution and sign under the actual runtime decode mode, then derive the anti-alias delta bound from an evidenced speed envelope
promotion_requirements.imu.*: measure the MPU6050 sensing origin relative to the model body origin and register the sensor axes to the body frame
promotion_requirements.actuator.*: use bounded bench/system-identification data with command, battery voltage, encoder state, and timestamps; torque gain requires direct torque evidence or dynamic identification with accepted inertial parameters
